# Verification analysis: outbound-nat-mapping-almalinux9

Job: `2026-09-05__12-23-47`

This report explains the verifier decisions recorded for this job. It interprets the saved evidence; it does not rerun the task or independently inspect the expired clusters.

## Task

> `node1` routes between `lan-a` and `lan-b`. When `node2` on `lan-a` opens a
> connection to `node3` on `lan-b`, have `node3` observe it as arriving from
> an address of your choosing on `node1` rather than from `node2`'s own
> address, while connections in the other direction keep their original
> source.

## Environment

- Systems: **1 opnsense + 2 almalinux9**
- Networks: **mgmt, lan-a, lan-b**
- Control node: **node2**
- Executor model: **claude-sonnet-5**

## Trial `outbound-nat-mapping-almalinux9__kXbtRwc`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The executor correctly implemented directional outbound SNAT on node1 (OPNsense) so that node2->node3 traffic is source-translated to node1's lan-b address (10.60.20.1) while node3->node2 traffic keeps node3's original source address. This was demonstrated with live TCP connections both before and after the NAT rule was applied, and re-verified after all three nodes (node2, node3, node1) were individually restarted with directly observed boot-identity changes matching the fixed lifecycle snapshots, followed by confirmed recovery of interfaces, firewall/NAT rules, and end-to-end NAT behavior. All material task outcomes and the independent restart-evidence protocol are satisfied. Hygiene is moderate: one NAT-placement mistake was self-corrected with no lasting effect, but test-listener services, opened firewalld ports, and config backup files were left running/present on the managed nodes at the end of the run rather than cleaned up.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.600 | 0.920 | 83/12 (+8 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **req-1 — Satisfied:** node2 (lan-a) -> node3 (lan-b) connections observed by node3 as arriving from a chosen address on node1, not node2's own address
  - **Why:** Baseline TCP test (cmd-0c9b62102bf8422d, node3 conns log cmd-ea06e0295fae4802) showed node3 seeing the real node2 address (10.60.10.2) before the SNAT rule existed. After the directional SNAT rule (interface opt2, source_net opt1, target 10.60.20.1) was installed and confirmed active in pf (cmd-fdd0ee6b9ffd42fe: 'nat on vtnet2 inet from (vtnet1:network) to any -> 10.60.20.1'), a fresh connection (cmd-ace9b669045e464f) and node3's connection log (cmd-ea06e0295fae4802) showed the source as 10.60.20.1 -- node1's chosen lan-b address. This was re-verified after each of the three node restarts (cmd-9e0a3af2a5834e19, cmd-4427d6ec3c234cd3, cmd-4a91711312c442c3), consistently showing 10.60.20.1 as the observed source.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-0c9b62102bf8422d`, `cmd-ea06e0295fae4802`, `cmd-fdd0ee6b9ffd42fe`, `cmd-ace9b669045e464f`, `cmd-9e0a3af2a5834e19`, `cmd-4427d6ec3c234cd3`, `cmd-4a91711312c442c3`
- **req-2 — Satisfied:** Connections in the reverse direction (node3 lan-b -> node2 lan-a) keep their original source address (no NAT applied)
  - **Why:** Baseline reverse connection (cmd-668e9640cd454ed0) showed node2 observing node3's real address (10.60.20.2). After the SNAT rule for the opposite direction (lan-a->lan-b only) was installed, the reverse-direction test (cmd-8e61d06b46784afe) and node2's connection log (cmd-6c89b8d55ac945ae) continued to show the unmodified source 10.60.20.2, confirming asymmetric behavior. Re-verified after each restart (cmd-f0652c983d3c43b8, cmd-6780975e1b1a4040, cmd-b27a8cdd1abc4751), always showing 10.60.20.2 unchanged.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-668e9640cd454ed0`, `cmd-8e61d06b46784afe`, `cmd-6c89b8d55ac945ae`, `cmd-f0652c983d3c43b8`, `cmd-6780975e1b1a4040`, `cmd-b27a8cdd1abc4751`
- **req-3 — Satisfied:** SNAT rule correctly implemented as outbound source translation (not accidentally a port-forward/DNAT) and persisted in node1 configuration
  - **Why:** An initial rule was mistakenly placed under the legacy <nat><rule> section (cmd-b2e6ebc3cab6458f), which pfctl showed materialized as an 'rdr' (destination NAT/port-forward) rule rather than SNAT (cmd-6d06db05a52e484a). The executor detected this, removed the erroneous rule, and added a proper rule under OPNsense/Firewall/Filter/snatrules (cmd-8b187ff0808c4df4), after which pfctl -s nat showed the correct outbound SNAT line 'nat on vtnet2 inet from (vtnet1:network) to any -> 10.60.20.1' (cmd-fdd0ee6b9ffd42fe). Config persistence was confirmed via config.xml inspection showing opt1/opt2 interfaces, hybrid NAT mode, and 1 snatrules entry (cmd-3899f7587d104680), and this rule was shown to auto-restore after node1's own reboot (cmd-0fcd30a2dec04493).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-b2e6ebc3cab6458f`, `cmd-6d06db05a52e484a`, `cmd-8b187ff0808c4df4`, `cmd-fdd0ee6b9ffd42fe`, `cmd-3899f7587d104680`, `cmd-0fcd30a2dec04493`
- **req-4 — Satisfied:** Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed for all three managed nodes with pre-restart baseline, restart, changed boot identity, and full recovery of NAT/data-plane behavior
  - **Why:** For node2: boot_id captured before (cmd-fddbdf7f26c94295: 9bdcc129...) and after reboot (cmd-36f1e211a3d4442a: c6fe83df...), matching the fixed after_executor snapshot; interface/route/firewalld state and NAT test behavior re-verified post-reboot (cmd-c1485032b3ff489c, cmd-9e0a3af2a5834e19). For node3: boot_id before (cmd-ae490fdce83c43ee: f54d7366...) and after (cmd-76a8c81aac43409e: c182563a...), matching fixed snapshot; recovery verified (cmd-ec226773369c45ab, cmd-4427d6ec3c234cd3). For node1 (FreeBSD): kern.boottime before (cmd-3899f7587d104680: 16:24:16) and after (cmd-bba0bc428ac84125: 16:30:25), matching the fixed after_executor snapshot value; full pf/interface/NAT rule auto-recovery and end-to-end NAT behavior reconfirmed post-reboot (cmd-0fcd30a2dec04493, cmd-4a91711312c442c3, cmd-b27a8cdd1abc4751). All three nodes show the required pre-restart healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, distinct post-restart boot identity, and recovered service/data/NAT state.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-fddbdf7f26c94295`, `cmd-36f1e211a3d4442a`, `cmd-c1485032b3ff489c`, `cmd-9e0a3af2a5834e19`, `cmd-ae490fdce83c43ee`, `cmd-76a8c81aac43409e`, `cmd-ec226773369c45ab`, `cmd-4427d6ec3c234cd3`, `cmd-3899f7587d104680`, `cmd-bba0bc428ac84125`, `cmd-0fcd30a2dec04493`, `cmd-4a91711312c442c3`, `cmd-b27a8cdd1abc4751`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.600**. Most executor mutations were necessary and correctly scoped: adding opt1/opt2 interfaces, filter pass rules, and the directional SNAT rule on node1; and configuring eth1 static IPs/routes on node2/node3 as a required prerequisite for testing cross-lan connectivity. One troubleshooting mistake occurred: cmd-b2e6ebc3cab6458f placed an outbound-NAT rule under the legacy <nat><rule> section, which pf revealed to be a DNAT/port-forward rather than SNAT (cmd-6d06db05a52e484a); this was corrected by removing the rule and adding a proper snatrules entry in cmd-8b187ff0808c4df4 -- a bounded, fully-reverted misstep with no lasting residue, but it should still be counted as an unnecessary mutation per policy. More significant residue: test echo-server listeners left permanently running after task completion on node2 (10.60.10.2:5001, python3 pid 849, cmd-dfc009afc6bb4035) and node3 (10.60.20.2:5000, python3 pid 836, cmd-e7fec28f91ff41ab), plus permanent firewalld port openings for 5000/tcp and 5001/tcp (cmd-4e8a98dc651644ec, cmd-65963d0fc6094e56, cmd-a50f4fa984ee4734, cmd-7eafb25488d14733) that remain in the after_executor listening-sockets snapshot -- these are verification artifacts, not part of the deliverable, and were not cleaned up, leaving open listening services and firewall exposure on both AlmaLinux nodes. Backup copies of config.xml (.bak1-.bak4) were also left on node1 without cleanup, though this is low-risk residue.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-b2e6ebc3cab6458f`, `cmd-6d06db05a52e484a`, `cmd-8b187ff0808c4df4`, `cmd-dfc009afc6bb4035`, `cmd-e7fec28f91ff41ab`, `cmd-4e8a98dc651644ec`, `cmd-65963d0fc6094e56`, `cmd-a50f4fa984ee4734`, `cmd-7eafb25488d14733`, `global:after_executor:node2:listening-sockets`, `global:after_executor:node3:listening-sockets`

### Comments and limitations

- Test echo-server processes and their opened firewalld ports (5000/tcp on node3, 5001/tcp on node2) were left active in the final state rather than torn down after verification.
- config.xml backup files (.bak1-.bak4) created on node1 during iterative edits were not observed to be cleaned up.
- No test was run to validate NAT/routing behavior for protocols other than TCP (e.g., ICMP end-to-end forwarding was attempted early but not re-verified after the NAT rule was finalized), though this is not central to the stated requirement.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.600); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.920; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
